title: Police copies of a DEA Form 106 filed in Massachusetts
rule_summary: If a person registered to distribute controlled substances discovers a theft or loss of controlled substances that requires the filing of DEA Form 106 with the United States Drug Enforcement Administration, the person shall simultaneously file a copy of that form with the department of state police. If a person registered to dispense controlled substances discovers such a theft or loss, the person shall simultaneously file a copy of that form with the police department in the city or town wherein the theft or loss is alleged to have occurred and with the department of state police.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate can name the police recipients and see that the copies are tied to the filing of the DEA Form 106 rather than to a period of their own.
common_confusions: A dispenser owes copies to both the local police department and the state police; a distributor owes a copy to the state police only.
The trigger is the filing of a DEA Form 106, so the copies travel with that filing rather than on a separate clock.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 15 on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed. A fresh independent audit is still required before any section relying on it is published.
